sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: One morning in March each year, I raise the window shades in my home
sentences.zh: 每年三月的一个早晨，我拉开家里的窗帘，

sentences.en: and see that the cherry tree outside has exploded into bloom.
sentences.zh: 看到外面的樱花树已经繁花盛开。

sentences.en: The tree has bare branches one day, a riot of delicate white flowers the next.
sentences.zh: 前一天树枝还光秃秃的，转眼间就开满了娇嫩的白花。

sentences.en: The last time this happened, the change was so spectacular
sentences.zh: 上一次看到这番景象时，变化之壮观，

sentences.en: that I reached for my phone to capture the moment.
sentences.zh: 让我忍不住拿起手机想记录下那一刻。

sentences.en: But the photo failed to show what my eyes had seen.
sentences.zh: 但照片却没能呈现出我眼中所见的一切。

sentences.en: For one thing, the camera included lots of details my brain ignored, stray branches, the edge of my windowsill.
sentences.zh: 首先，相机捕捉到了许多我大脑自动忽略的细节，比如杂乱的枝条、窗台的边缘。

sentences.en: The light in the picture was not as brilliant as it had appeared to me just moments earlier.
sentences.zh: 照片里的光线也不如我刚才亲眼所见的那样灿烂。

sentences.en: More importantly, the image didn't capture the meaning my brain perceived when I saw the tree in bloom.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，这张照片没能捕捉到我看到樱花盛开时，大脑所感知到的那种意义。

sentences.en: The message that winter was nearly over, that spring was around the corner.
sentences.zh: 那种冬天即将结束、春天就在眼前的讯息。

sentences.en: Let me now ask you a question.
sentences.zh: 现在让我问你一个问题。

sentences.en: Which version of the cherry tree represents reality better?
sentences.zh: 哪一个版本的樱花树更能代表现实？

sentences.en: The one in the photo or the one inside my head?
sentences.zh: 是照片里的那棵，还是我脑海里的那棵？

sentences.en: Today we launch a two-part series that explores what happens when two ways of understanding
sentences.zh: 今天我们开启一个两部分的系列节目，探讨当两种认知方式

sentences.en: come into conflict with each other.
sentences.zh: 发生冲突时会发生什么。

sentences.en: One is objective, the other subjective.
sentences.zh: 一种是客观的，另一种是主观的。

sentences.en: One aims for precision, the other is attentive to meaning.
sentences.zh: 一种追求精确，另一种关注意义。

sentences.en: Each can be bewildered, even suspicious, of the other.
sentences.zh: 两者可能都会对对方感到困惑，甚至怀疑。

sentences.en: Two Ways of Seeing, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》为您带来“两种观察方式”。

sentences.en: Richard Davidson grew up in Brooklyn during the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 理查德·戴维森在20世纪60年代的布鲁克林长大。

sentences.en: When he was in high school, he came across an article in the magazine Science News about a study.
sentences.zh: 上高中时，他在《科学新闻》杂志上偶然看到了一篇关于某项研究的文章。

sentences.en: I had read about a sleep laboratory that was based in a hospital in Brooklyn,
sentences.zh: 我读到了一家位于布鲁克林医院的睡眠实验室，

sentences.en: Maimonides Hospital, actually the hospital that I was born in.
sentences.zh: 就是迈蒙尼德医院，其实那也是我出生的医院。

sentences.en: Ritchie called the hospital to ask if he might be able to volunteer in the lab.
sentences.zh: 里奇打电话给医院，询问是否可以去实验室做志愿者。

sentences.en: You know, I talked to some receptionist who kind of dismissed me, and it took more persistence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我跟一位接待员谈过，她有点打发我，所以我必须更加坚持。

sentences.en: I actually wrote a letter, a handwritten letter, and then followed it up with another phone call.
sentences.zh: 我真的写了一封信，一封手写信，然后又跟进打了一个电话。

sentences.en: And although they had never had a high school volunteer before, we were able to work out an arrangement.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们以前从未招过高中生志愿者，但我们还是达成了一项安排。

sentences.en: In the afternoons after school, while other kids were playing sports or doing homework,
sentences.zh: 每天放学后的下午，当其他孩子在做运动或写作业时，

sentences.en: Ritchie would take the subway to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 里奇就会坐地铁去医院。

sentences.en: He got to help around the lab, doing basic work, like cleaning electrodes.
sentences.zh: 他可以在实验室帮忙做些基础工作，比如清洁电极。

sentences.en: But one time, he got permission from his parents to stay up all night and watch the scientists in action.
sentences.zh: 但有一次，他获得了父母的许可，通宵留下来观察科学家们的工作。

sentences.en: The research subject was sleeping in another room that was adjacent to the room that I was in.
sentences.zh: 研究对象睡在隔壁房间，我就在那个房间里。

sentences.en: It had a bed, and they were wired up.
sentences.zh: 那里有一张床，他们身上连着线。

sentences.en: So they were recorded for brain electrical activity measurement.
sentences.zh: 他们被记录下来以测量大脑的电活动。

sentences.en: Also, electrodes were on their eyes to record eye movements.
sentences.zh: 此外，眼睛上也贴了电极以记录眼球运动。

sentences.en: And so I saw the electrodes being put on, and I saw this person going to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我看着电极被贴上，看着那个人入睡。

sentences.en: The scientists would let the person drift into dreams, the REM cycle.
sentences.zh: 科学家们会让受试者进入梦境，即快速眼动睡眠周期。

sentences.en: And then a person was awakened and asked, was there anything going through your mind just before we awakened you?
sentences.zh: 然后把人叫醒，问他们：“在我们叫醒你之前，你脑子里在想什么吗？”

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the interesting things is that although most people don't remember their dreams,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有趣的一点是，虽然大多数人记不住自己的梦，

sentences.en: when you wake a person up immediately after a REM period like this, typically you do get recall in the vast majority of cases.
sentences.zh: 但当你像这样在快速眼动期结束后立即叫醒一个人时，绝大多数情况下他们都能回忆起来。

sentences.en: What was amazing to Ritchie was that scientists could learn about the dream in two completely different ways.
sentences.zh: 让里奇感到惊奇的是，科学家们可以通过两种截然不同的方式来了解梦境。

sentences.en: They could objectively measure the dreamer's eye movements and capture patterns of brain activity.
sentences.zh: 他们可以客观地测量做梦者的眼球运动并捕捉大脑活动的模式。

sentences.en: But they could also match this objective data with the dreamer's subjective account of the dream.
sentences.zh: 但他们也可以将这些客观数据与做梦者对梦境的主观描述进行比对。

sentences.en: You know, I was just more taken with the whole process that here is a strategy
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是被整个过程深深吸引了，这里竟然有一种策略

sentences.en: for looking at the physiological correlates of mental experience.
sentences.zh: 可以用来观察心理体验的生理相关性。

sentences.en: And this was a way to study this.
sentences.zh: 这是一种研究方法。

sentences.en: It was a whole kind of paradigm that was unfolding before me
sentences.zh: 这是一种在我面前展开的全新范式，

sentences.en: that I had never thought about before.
sentences.zh: 是我以前从未想过的。

sentences.en: And it was super exciting to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: It was exciting for Ritchie at age 14, and it was revolutionary for the time.
sentences.zh: 这对14岁的里奇来说很兴奋，在当时也是革命性的。

sentences.en: For centuries, the main way to understand someone's thoughts
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，了解他人想法的主要方式

sentences.en: was to simply ask them.
sentences.zh: 就是直接询问他们。

sentences.en: The person would describe what was happening inside their head.
sentences.zh: 那个人会描述他们脑子里正在发生什么。

sentences.en: But we humans are prone to bias and blind spots,
sentences.zh: 但我们人类容易产生偏见和盲点，

sentences.en: forgetfulness and vanity.
sentences.zh: 容易健忘和虚荣。

sentences.en: Everyone from scientists to marketers to political consultants know
sentences.zh: 从科学家到营销人员再到政治顾问，每个人都知道，

sentences.en: if you really want to learn people's preferences,
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想了解人们的偏好，

sentences.en: you should observe how they behave
sentences.zh: 你应该观察他们的行为，

sentences.en: rather than listen to what they say.
sentences.zh: 而不是听他们说了什么。

sentences.en: With the brain measurement technologies Ritchie saw at the lab
sentences.zh: 随着里奇在实验室看到的脑部测量技术出现，

sentences.en: came a new way to study the mind objectively.
sentences.zh: 一种客观研究思维的新方法诞生了，

sentences.en: from the outside in.
sentences.zh: 即从外部向内观察。

sentences.en: Here was a situation where there was simultaneously a distinct change in the
sentences.zh: 这是一种情况，大脑中同时发生了明显的变化，

sentences.en: brain that was accompanied by a report of a conscious experience, a mental experience.
sentences.zh: 并伴随着对意识体验、心理体验的报告。

sentences.en: And that to me was just mind-blowing and captured my imagination.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直太震撼了，深深抓住了我的想象力。

sentences.en: And really at age 14,
sentences.zh: 真的，在14岁那年，

sentences.en: as corny it is to say, I knew that my life was somehow going to be dedicated to the study of the
sentences.zh: 虽然说出来有点老套，但我知道我的余生注定要致力于研究

sentences.en: mind.
sentences.zh: 思维。

sentences.en: I did not know what specific path I would take, but I knew that the mind was really essential
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体会走哪条路，但我知道思维对我们所做的一切都至关重要，

sentences.en: to everything that we do, and that that was really the most important thing that I can dedicate
sentences.zh: 那确实是我能全身心投入的最重要的事情。

sentences.en: myself to.
sentences.zh: 最终，里奇成为了学习这两种理解思维技术的学生。

sentences.en: In time, Richie was to become a student of two techniques to understand the mind.
sentences.zh: 一种

sentences.en: One
sentences.zh: 技术试图从内部向外理解思维。

sentences.en: technique tried to understand the mind from the inside out.
sentences.zh: 它通过将注意力的聚光灯转向内心，

sentences.en: It paid attention to the variety and
sentences.zh: 来关注心理体验的多样性和

sentences.en: complexity of mental experiences by turning the spotlight of attention inward.
sentences.zh: 复杂性。

sentences.en: This approach would
sentences.zh: 这种方法会

sentences.en: say that my subjective appraisal of the cherry tree represented reality more accurately.
sentences.zh: 认为我对樱花树的主观评价更准确地代表了现实。

sentences.en: The other
sentences.zh: 另一种

sentences.en: technique said, the mind could best be understood by studying it from the outside, using scientific
sentences.zh: 技术则认为，通过使用科学工具和科学方法从外部研究思维，才能最好地理解它。

sentences.en: tools and the scientific method.
sentences.zh: 其目标是尽可能消除主观评价，

sentences.en: The goal was to eliminate subjective appraisal as much as possible,
sentences.zh: 因为，特别是在向内审视时，自我感知往往是有缺陷且不可靠的。

sentences.en: because, especially when it came to looking inward, self-perception was flawed and flaky.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考自己的思维时，就像站在镜子大厅里一样。

sentences.en: When we think about our own minds, it's like standing in a hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 我们无法分辨

sentences.en: We cannot tell
sentences.zh: 哪里是现实的终点，哪里是倒影的起点。

sentences.en: where reality ends and reflection begins.
sentences.zh: 里奇发现自己无法抗拒地被这两种技术所吸引。

sentences.en: Ritchie found himself irresistibly drawn to both techniques.
sentences.zh: 他觉得每一种技术都能给另一种带来很多启示。

sentences.en: He felt each had much to teach the other.
sentences.zh: 他很快就会了解到，每种技术的实践者

sentences.en: He was soon to learn the many ways
sentences.zh: 对另一种技术

sentences.en: that practitioners of each technique
sentences.zh: 都会保持深深的警惕。

sentences.en: would be deeply wary of the other.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个少年时，

sentences.en: When I was a teenager,
sentences.zh: 我记得曾和朋友们讨论过一个著名的思想实验。

sentences.en: I remember discussing a famous thought experiment with friends.
sentences.zh: 中国的一位哲学家睡着了，梦见自己变成了一只蝴蝶。

sentences.en: A philosopher in China went to sleep and dreamed he was a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 他从一朵花飞到另一朵花，思考着蝴蝶的想法，啜饮着蝴蝶大小的花蜜。

sentences.en: He fluttered from flower to flower, thinking butterfly thoughts and taking butterfly-sized sips of nectar.
sentences.zh: 然后他醒了过来，意识到自己不是蝴蝶，而是一个梦见自己是蝴蝶的人。

sentences.en: Then he woke up and realized he wasn't a butterfly, but a man who had dreamed he was a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 下一刻，一个令人不安的想法出现在他脑海中。

sentences.en: The next moment, a disturbing thought occurred to him.
sentences.zh: 他在梦中确实感觉自己是一只蝴蝶。

sentences.en: He had really felt he was a butterfly in the dream.
sentences.zh: 他确信自己就是一只蝴蝶。

sentences.en: He was convinced he was a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 现在醒来后，他绝对确信自己不是蝴蝶，而是一个人。

sentences.en: Now, having woken up, he was absolutely convinced he was not a butterfly, but a man.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人可以梦见自己是蝴蝶，

sentences.en: If a man could dream that he was a butterfly,
sentences.zh: 那么有没有可能他现在是一只梦见自己是人的蝴蝶呢？

sentences.en: was it not possible that he was now a butterfly dreaming that he was a man?
sentences.zh: 这个思想实验揭示了一个深刻的真理。

sentences.en: The thought experiment reveals a deep truth.
sentences.zh: 我们所感知的现实，无法脱离我们自身思维的运作。

sentences.en: What we perceive as reality cannot be extricated from the workings of our own mind.
sentences.zh: 我们所体验的世界实际上是由我们的思维和大脑构建的，所以，

sentences.en: the world that we experience is actually constructed by our minds and our brains and so
sentences.zh: 是的，外面确实有事物存在，但我们感知那些事物的方式，

sentences.en: yeah there are things out there but the way we perceive those things that are out there
sentences.zh: 完全取决于我们如何在各自的思维和大脑中构建它们，所以，

sentences.en: is entirely a function of how we construct it in our own individual minds and brains and so
sentences.zh: 如果我们能以不同的方式构建它，我们确实可以生活在一个不同的世界里。

sentences.en: if we can construct it differently we can literally live in a different world
sentences.zh: 随着理查德·戴维森长大成人，他开始对自己的思维如何构建现实产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: As Ritchie Davidson came of age, he became very interested in how his mind constructed reality.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代的反主流文化运动正如火如荼。

sentences.en: The counterculture movement of the 1960s was in full swing.
sentences.zh: 像吉姆·莫里森这样的音乐家正在探索如何穿透自我感知的面纱并实现突破。

sentences.en: Musicians like Jim Morrison were exploring how you could pierce the veil of your own perception and break through.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是60年代的产物，那种文化对我的人生有着非常重要的影响。

sentences.en: I was definitely a product of the 60s, and the culture was very much an important influence on my life.
sentences.zh: 它就像弥漫在空气中一样。

sentences.en: It was sort of in the air.
sentences.zh: 我非常迷恋披头士乐队和其他正在尝试探索思维的音乐团体，并考虑这样一种可能性：我们许多人从小被教导的看待世界的标准方式，

sentences.en: I was quite taken with the Beatles and other musical groups who were experimenting with their minds and considering the possibility that the kind of standard way that many of us were raised and taught to approach the world,
sentences.zh: 套用莎士比亚的话说，

sentences.en: to paraphrase Shakespeare,
sentences.zh: 天地间有许多事物，是你们的哲学所梦想不到的。

sentences.en: there are more things in heaven that are dreamt of in your philosophy.
sentences.zh: 像披头士这样的乐队邀请听众去测试自己思维的极限。

sentences.en: Bands like the Beatles invited listeners to test the limits of their own minds.
sentences.zh: 当他们唱起《露西在缀满钻石的天空》时，

sentences.en: When they sang Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds,
sentences.zh: 这被广泛认为是暗指致幻剂LSD。

sentences.en: this was widely perceived to be a reference to the hallucinogenic drug LSD.
sentences.zh: 我确实听过披头士的现场演出。

sentences.en: I did hear the Beatles live.
sentences.zh: 《露西在缀满钻石的天空》对我成长过程中确实是一首重要的歌。

sentences.en: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds was certainly an important song for me growing up.
sentences.zh: 哈佛心理学家蒂莫西·利里当时正在进行迷幻蘑菇实验，

sentences.en: The Harvard psychologist Timothy Leary was experimenting with magic mushrooms
sentences.zh: 并鼓励志愿者和研究人员探索迷幻药物。

sentences.en: and encouraging volunteers and studies to explore psychedelic drugs.
sentences.zh: 1967年，他在旧金山金门公园对3万名嬉皮士发表了演讲。

sentences.en: In 1967, he spoke to a group of 30,000 hippies at San Francisco's Golden Gate Park.
sentences.zh: 他敦促他们“开启、调频、退出”。

sentences.en: He urged them to turn on, tune in, and drop out.
sentences.zh: 1968年，披头士乐队前往印度，向一位名叫玛哈礼希·玛赫西·优济的冥想大师学习。

sentences.en: In 1968, the Beatles went to India to learn from a meditation master named Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.
sentences.zh: 尤其是吉他手乔治·哈里森，

sentences.en: Guitarist George Harrison, in particular,
sentences.zh: 对当时所谓的“超觉静坐”产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: developed a deep interest in what was known at the time as transcendental meditation.
sentences.zh: 里奇对这些想法很着迷。

sentences.en: Ritchie was fascinated by these ideas.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，他发现自己被一个相关的概念所吸引。

sentences.en: But increasingly, he found himself drawn to a related concept.
sentences.zh: 我们思维内部发生的事情并不会停留在思维内部。

sentences.en: What happens inside our minds doesn't stay inside our minds.
sentences.zh: 我们思考的思想、我们拥有的感受，

sentences.en: The thoughts we think, the feelings we have,
sentences.zh: 可以塑造并影响我们所生活的世界。

sentences.en: can shape and influence the world in which we live.
sentences.zh: 我们的思维与这个破碎的世界状态之间存在着联系。

sentences.en: There was a link between our minds and the broken state of the world.

sentences.en: Some of John Lennon's songs specifically,
sentences.zh: 《想象》在那张专辑里确实是一首很重要的歌。

sentences.en: Imagine was really an important song in that whole album.
sentences.zh: 那种认为所有人类都能获得一种不同生存方式的想法，

sentences.en: The idea that there is a different way of being that is accessible to all humans,
sentences.zh: 我想说，那是一种充满更多和平、同情、善良和爱的生存方式。

sentences.en: And I would say a way of being that is imbued with greater peace and compassion and kindness and love.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多方面，这些主题在今天依然具有现实意义。

sentences.en: You know, in many ways, those are still the relevant themes today.
sentences.zh: 那么，这里的动力是对思维的好奇心吗？

sentences.en: And was the impulse here a curiosity about the mind?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这种动力更多是由想要看到一个不同世界的愿望所塑造的？

sentences.en: Or was it an impulse that was shaped more by wanting to see a different kind of world?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当我想到《露西在缀满钻石的天空》和《想象》时，

sentences.en: In other words, when I think about Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds and I think about Imagine,
